providers.contract:
Compute shape variation of conditional distributions P(Y|X=x) across bins.

For each bin of X, computes the conditional distribution P(Y|X=x) as a
histogram, mean-centers them, and returns the overall standard deviation.
For numerical data with few unique values, uses cross-correlation
alignment to detrend the location shift (the deterministic function f(x))
before comparing shapes.

This goes beyond moment-based comparisons by capturing the full
distributional shape variation.

Args:
    x: Cause candidate variable, shape (n,).
    tx: Type descriptor for x.
    y: Effect candidate variable, shape (n,).
    ty: Type descriptor for y.
    ffactor: Bin granularity factor (default 2 for this atom).
    maxdev: Maximum standard deviations for clipping.
    minc: Minimum samples per bin to include.

Returns:
    Std of mean-centered conditional distributions. Lower in the causal
    direction.

Compute the standard deviation of conditional kurtosis of Y|X=x across bins.

Kurtosis captures fourth-moment structure of the noise distribution. In
the causal direction, kurtosis should be stable (constant noise). In the
anti-causal direction, the mixing of signal and noise produces varying
tail behavior.

Args:
    x: Cause candidate variable, shape (n,).
    tx: Type descriptor for x.
    y: Effect candidate variable, shape (n,).
    ty: Type descriptor for y.
    ffactor: Bin granularity factor.
    maxdev: Maximum standard deviations for clipping.
    minc: Minimum samples per bin to include.

Returns:
    Std of conditional kurtosis values. Lower in the causal direction.

Compute the standard deviation of conditional skewness of Y|X=x across bins.

Skewness variation is a higher-order diagnostic than entropy variation.
It detects asymmetries in the conditional noise distribution that entropy
(a symmetric measure) may miss, particularly in non-Gaussian settings.

Args:
    x: Cause candidate variable, shape (n,).
    tx: Type descriptor for x.
    y: Effect candidate variable, shape (n,).
    ty: Type descriptor for y.
    ffactor: Bin granularity factor.
    maxdev: Maximum standard deviations for clipping.
    minc: Minimum samples per bin to include.

Returns:
    Std of conditional skewness values. Lower in the causal direction.

Evaluate the source fit_noise_entropy definition on discretized X and Y.

Include X bins with strictly more than minc samples. Compute bias-corrected
discrete entropy of discretized Y in each bin and divide their standard
deviation by log of the source-defined discretized Y alphabet size.
Returns zero when no X bin qualifies or the Y alphabet has one value.
Distinct from the older atom that measures entropy of raw Y values.
Source: jarfo/cause-effect features.py, fit_noise_entropy.

Combine left (X→Y) and right (Y→X) classifier scores by differencing.

Trains two separate binary classifiers — one for "is X→Y?" and one for
"is Y→X?" — then takes their difference as the causal score. This avoids
forcing a single classifier to learn both the independence boundary and
the direction boundary simultaneously.

Args:
    left_scores: P(X→Y) from the left classifier, shape (2n,).
    right_scores: P(Y→X) from the right classifier, shape (2n,).
    symmetrize: Whether to enforce paired antisymmetry (default True).

Returns:
    Causal direction scores, shape (2n,). Positive = X→Y.

Enforce antisymmetry on paired causal direction predictions.

For each adjacent pair of predictions (A→B, B→A), sets:
    score[A→B] = (pred[A→B] - pred[B→A]) / 2
    score[B→A] = -score[A→B]

This enforces the physical constraint that score(A→B) = -score(B→A),
doubling the effective data and removing any classifier bias toward
consistently predicting positive or negative. Only the asymmetric
signal survives.

Expects predictions to be ordered as alternating pairs:
[pred(A1→B1), pred(B1→A1), pred(A2→B2), pred(B2→A2), ...].

Args:
    predictions: Raw classifier predictions, shape (2n,).

Returns:
    Antisymmetrized predictions, shape (2n,).

Combine independence and direction scores via multiplicative gating.

Decomposes causal inference into two stages:
1. Independence: P(dependent) — are the variables related at all?
2. Direction: which way does the causal arrow point?

The final score is P(dependent) * direction_score. This means
independent pairs get scores near 0 regardless of the direction
classifier output — architecturally principled because you should
not assign a causal direction to independent variables.

When symmetrize=True, independence scores are averaged across each
pair and direction scores are antisymmetrized.

Args:
    independence_scores: P(dependent) from the independence classifier,
        shape (2n,). Values should be in [0, 1].
    direction_scores: Raw direction predictions, shape (2n,).
    symmetrize: Whether to enforce paired symmetry (default True).

Returns:
    Combined causal scores, shape (2n,).

Combine predictions from multiple estimators via weighted average.

When weights are provided, computes the weighted dot product.
When weights are None, returns the unweighted stack for downstream
processing.

The three estimator architectures (ID, Symmetric, OneStep) have
different inductive biases, and their combination provides robustness
against misspecification of any single model.

Args:
    prediction_arrays: List of prediction arrays, each shape (n,).
    weights: Optional weight vector, shape (k,). If None, returns
        the stacked array.

Returns:
    Combined predictions, shape (n,) if weighted, or (k, n) if unweighted.

Combine three paired causal score vectors with explicit graph ports.

All scores must be finite, nonempty, equally shaped 1D arrays in [-1,1]
with adjacent-pair antisymmetry (absolute tolerance 1e-8). Weights follow
independence/direction, left/right, one-step order and must be three finite
nonnegative values summing to one within 1e-8. No normalization is performed.
Delegates the weighted sum to the existing ensemble implementation.
This adapter combines predictions; it does not fit or evaluate classifiers.

Select P(label=1) from a binary {0,1} or {-1,1} classifier.

Explicit labels determine column order. Reject nonfinite, negative,
nonnormalized or otherwise malformed distributions. Does not rescale
a binary probability into a signed score or infer classifier semantics.

Return P(label=1) minus P(label=-1) for each classifier prediction.

Rows are predictions; the three columns correspond to the supplied labels
-1, 0 and 1 in any order. Label 0 denotes independence. Inputs must be finite
real numeric arrays, with probabilities in [0,1] and each row summing to one
within absolute tolerance 1e-8. Invalid distributions are rejected without
normalization. Returns a float64 vector in [-1,1], without input mutation.

This implements the three-class score conversion used by the upstream
cause-effect estimator. It does not train a classifier, establish causality,
or enforce symmetry between reversed observation pairs.

Source: https://github.com/jarfo/cause-effect/blob/master/estimator.py
(Pipeline.predict, three-class probability conversion).

Discretize a continuous variable into integer bins with robust normalization.

Two-pass normalization: first pass identifies inliers within maxdev
standard deviations, second pass re-centers/re-scales using only those
inliers. This prevents outliers from distorting the binning.

Args:
    x: Variable samples, shape (n,).
    tx: Variable type.
    ffactor: Bins per standard deviation (default 3 → 19 bins total).
    maxdev: Maximum standard deviations for clipping.
    norm: Whether to apply normalization.

Returns:
    Discretized values, shape (n,).

Compute the Hilbert-Schmidt Independence Criterion (HSIC) test statistic.

Measures statistical dependence between X and Y using RBF kernels with
automatic median-distance bandwidth selection (Gretton et al., 2005).
HSIC = (1/m) * trace(K_c @ L_c) where K_c, L_c are centered kernel
matrices.

Uses evenly-spaced subsampling (not random) when n > maxpnt to preserve
distribution shape while keeping the O(n^2) kernel computation tractable.

Args:
    X: First variable, shape (n,) or (n, d).
    Y: Second variable, shape (n,) or (n, d).
    sig: Kernel bandwidths [sig_x, sig_y]. Use -1 for median heuristic.
    maxpnt: Maximum points for subsampling.

Returns:
    HSIC test statistic. Higher values indicate stronger dependence.

Compute the Information-Geometric Causal Inference (IGCI) asymmetry score.

Sorts samples by x, computes the log-ratio of consecutive x-deltas to
y-deltas. Under the IGCI framework (Daniusis et al., 2012), if X causes
Y via a deterministic function, the distribution of the slope (Jacobian)
is independent of the cause distribution. The score is asymmetric:
igci(X, Y) != igci(Y, X), and the difference indicates causal direction.

Handles non-injective mappings by averaging y values per unique x, and
weights log-ratios by the minimum count of adjacent bins.

Args:
    x: Cause candidate variable, shape (n,).
    tx: Type of x (BINARY, CATEGORICAL, or NUMERICAL).
    y: Effect candidate variable, shape (n,).
    ty: Type of y.

Returns:
    IGCI asymmetry score. Compute igci(X,Y) - igci(Y,X) for direction.

Estimate differential entropy using a k-nearest-neighbor approach.

Kozachenko-Leonenko type estimator adapted for mixed discrete/continuous
data. Groups identical values, computes inter-point spacings weighted by
counts, and applies digamma bias corrections.

Args:
    x: Variable samples, shape (n,).
    tx: Variable type.
    m: KNN neighbor count for spacing estimation.

Returns:
    Estimated differential entropy (nats).

Compute normalized Bayesian error rate of predicting Y from X.

Discretizes both variables, constructs the joint probability table, and
computes the MAP error rate normalized by the maximum possible error rate.
The asymmetry nep(X→Y) != nep(Y→X) provides causal signal because the
cause typically has lower normalized error in predicting the effect.

Args:
    x: Predictor variable, shape (n,).
    tx: Type of x.
    y: Target variable, shape (n,).
    ty: Type of y.
    ffactor: Bin granularity factor (bins per standard deviation).
    maxdev: Maximum deviations for clipping.

Returns:
    Normalized error probability in [0, 1].

Quantify nonlinearity asymmetry between X→Y and Y→X polynomial fits.

Fits degree-1 and degree-2 polynomials from X to Y, then returns
|2*a2| + |a2_1 - a1_0| where a2 is the quadratic coefficient and a2_1,
a1_0 are the linear coefficients from degree-2 and degree-1 fits.

Causal mechanisms tend to be "simpler" in the forward direction. If
X→Y is approximately linear but Y→X is nonlinear, the difference
signals the causal direction.

Args:
    x: Cause candidate, shape (n,).
    tx: Type of x.
    y: Effect candidate, shape (n,).
    ty: Type of y.

Returns:
    Nonlinearity score. Compute fit(X,Y) - fit(Y,X) for direction.

Compute polynomial regression residual standard deviation.

Fits a degree-m polynomial from X to Y and returns the residual std.
Type-aware: categorical X is converted via mean-of-Y encoding.
The asymmetry fit_error(X→Y) - fit_error(Y→X) implements a practical
additive noise model test.

Args:
    x: Predictor variable, shape (n,).
    tx: Type of x.
    y: Target variable, shape (n,).
    ty: Type of y.
    m: Polynomial degree.

Returns:
    Standard deviation of residuals.

Compute KL-divergence-like measure from the empirical distribution to uniform.

Under the independence of cause and mechanism principle (Lemeire & Janzing,
2012), the cause distribution tends to be "simpler" (closer to uniform).
The asymmetry between uniform_divergence(X) and uniform_divergence(Y)
indicates which variable is more likely the cause.

Uses a KNN density estimate with variable-width bins.

Args:
    x: Variable samples, shape (n,).
    tx: Variable type.
    m: Neighbor count for density estimation.

Returns:
    Divergence from uniform. Lower values suggest the variable is a cause.

Compute one named statistic serially for each aligned typed pair.

Every variable is a finite, nonconstant real vector with at least three
samples; Binary has exactly two values. Pair lengths match, but may vary
across rows. Explicit Numerical/Categorical/Binary types retain the reviewed
scalar algorithms' conventions, including frequency-rank normalization,
categorical dependence dispatch and 0.7-corrected binned entropy. These
conventions are part of this version's contract, not inferred from data.
No labels or population-wide statistics are used. Undefined/nonfinite
results are rejected. A returned statistic is not proof of causality.

Assemble all 43 explicitly supplied columns in fixed source recipe order.

Every numerical statistic is computed upstream; this adapter only fixes
column order and delegates finite, aligned matrix assembly to a generic atom.
Return one explicit statistic name per source-selected feature column.
Route independently named populations to shared generic pair interfaces.

Interleave each {-1,0,+1} integer label with its signed negation.

Requires one label per nonempty input pair list; observations are not read.
Converts to int64 before negation, including unsigned inputs, so reverse
labels cannot wrap to large positive values. Does not modify caller labels.

Validate then expose adjacent forward/reverse samples and explicit types.

Returns four aligned lists: x samples, x types, y samples, y types. Each
input pair contributes (x,y) then (y,x). Vectors may differ in length across
pairs; within a pair lengths match and are at least three. Samples are
finite real and nonconstant; Binary requires exactly two observed values.
Copies every output array into float64. Computes no statistics or features.

Check source role label sets and return the same five models unchanged.

Requires fitted sklearn GradientBoostingClassifiers. One-step labels are
{-1,0,1}; direction labels are {-1,1}; independence/left/right are {0,1}.
No probabilities are computed and no model is trained, copied or mutated.
Actual generic prediction nodes check feature widths and finite outputs.
Shape-only model metadata cannot prove these label contracts.

Return explicit (features, labels, weights) ports for each source role.

Flattened order is one-step, independence, direction, left, right. Uses
the reviewed source partition rules, including adjacent reversed labels,
exclusion of independent rows from direction training, unit direction
weights and negative-class balancing for the three binary indicator tasks.
One-step weights remain None. No fitting or prediction occurs here.
This is a recipe adapter; the downstream weighted fitter is generic.
All arrays are copied so one consumer cannot mutate another role's inputs.
Abstract-only shape propagation is unsupported because direction row count
depends on actual labels; concrete execution remains supported.

Predict probabilities and return a copy of their corresponding class labels.

Requires an in-memory fitted sklearn GradientBoostingClassifier and a finite
real, nonempty feature matrix with the trained number of columns. The model
is supplied by the caller; this function does not fit or deserialize models.
Class order comes from classes_, never an assumed ordering. Prediction
semantics follow sklearn's public predict_proba API.

Fit one in-memory classifier with explicit labels and optional weights.

Accepts a finite nonempty real matrix and an aligned integer label vector
containing at least two classes. Labels are arbitrary integers; there are no
causal roles, paired-row assumptions, feature recipes or balancing rules.
Optional weights must be finite, strictly positive and aligned. None is
passed through unchanged. Uses sklearn log_loss and explicit deterministic
settings; native thread pools are limited to one for this fit. Returns the
fitted model without reading or writing files or mutating caller arrays.
Zero/negative weights, missing values and single-class fits are outside this
version's contract. No prediction quality or historical-library claim.

Natural-log empirical entropy with optional finite-count correction.

Each scalar (1D) or entire row (2D) is a discrete symbol; finite real values
are compared exactly, without binning. Returns -sum(p log p) plus
correction*(observed_symbols-1)/(2*sample_count). Correction must be finite
and nonnegative; zero is the ordinary plug-in estimator. Keeps first-seen
symbol order for reproducible summation. No task or distribution inference.

Mean of x**x_power * y**y_power for aligned finite real vectors.

Powers are nonnegative integers. Inputs are converted to float64 before
exponentiation, preventing integer overflow. No centering or scaling is
performed: callers supply normalized samples when that is their intended
statistic. Rejects nonfinite arithmetic and leaves inputs unchanged.

Stack finite real vectors in caller-specified column order, without fitting.

Every column must have the same positive row count. No feature selection,
name inference, normalization, imputation or broadcasting occurs. Output is
a new float64 matrix. Column semantics and row alignment belong to callers.

limitations: Native signatures and graph aliases reviewed; stored catalog ports still need comparison
Indirect scalar output name result is a proposed alias, not a claim about existing catalog names
Native docstrings describe contracts; semantic, bounds and transaction reviews remain required
